title: Sort Without Copy
goal: Alphabetical order, zero clones — and beware the key that lies.
hints: sort_by_key clones every element into a key — but the elements ARE the keys.
Sorting by length compiles happily. Check what the test expects before celebrating.
explanation: sort_by_key(|n| n.clone()) builds an owned copy of every String just to compare them — but when the sort key is the element itself, plain .sort() compares in place with zero allocations. The length-key variant is the deeper trap: it compiles and runs, but sorts by the wrong property entirely — ["zoe","amy","mia"] all have length 3, so nothing moves. Compiling is not the same as correct.
